Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Titan Aerospace & Defense Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, today's conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the conference over to John Smith, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Titan Aerospace & Defense's Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me today are David Johnson, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Operating Officer; and Lisa Patel, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

David Johnson:
Thank you, John, and good morning, everyone. Titan Aerospace & Defense delivered a solid performance in Q2, demonstrating the resilience of our business model and the strength of our diversified portfolio across commercial aerospace, defense systems, space, and propulsion. Our priorities remain focused on executing our strategy, driving operational excellence, and delivering value to our shareholders. We've seen robust gross margin expansion through disciplined program management, accelerating growth in our high-margin aftermarket and services business, significant backlog additions that provide multi-year revenue visibility, sustained R&D investments positioning us for next-generation leadership, and balanced revenue growth across all segments fueled by both commercial recovery and defense demand.

We are particularly excited about the recent advancements in our next-generation air dominance platform program—analogous to NGAD—and its potential to drive substantial future growth through collaborative combat aircraft demonstrators and advanced capabilities. We are seeing strong demand for our defense systems, including F-35 sustainment and hypersonic weapons, and our commercial aerospace business is recovering steadily with increased OEM deliveries and flight hours.

With that, I'll turn it over to Sarah for a deeper dive into our financial results.

Sarah Lee:
Thank you, David, and good morning, everyone. Now, let's turn to the financials. In Q2, we reported revenue of $18.7 billion, representing an 18% increase year-over-year, driven by execution across our key segments. Our earnings per share were $3.25 diluted. We continue to maintain a strong balance sheet with $5.2 billion in cash and equivalents. Our guidance for the full year remains unchanged at revenue of $72-75 billion, operating margins of 11.5-11.8%, and EPS of $13.00-13.50. We are actively managing our costs and investing in key growth initiatives. We are also focused on returning capital to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

Our specific financial highlights include gross margin of 14.2%, operating income of $2.2 billion, and free cash flow of $1.5 billion.

As we dive deeper into profitability metrics, we achieved gross margins of 14.2% for the quarter, expanding 70 basis points year-over-year from 13.5% and marking our third consecutive quarter of sequential improvement. This outperformance reflects disciplined program management and structural cost efficiencies. On the Defense side, our next-generation air dominance platform saw gross margins expand to 15.8%, up from 14.2% a year ago, thanks to favorable Estimate at Completion adjustments on three fixed-price development contracts totaling $2.4 billion. We proactively mitigated supply chain inflation on titanium forgings and composites by qualifying dual-sourced suppliers in Eastern Europe, reducing material cost variance by 12%.

In Space & Launch, margins held steady at 13.9%, benefiting from the ramp in our Vulcan Centaur heavy-lift vehicle production, now at full rate following certification. We absorbed some near-term pressure from propulsion qualification testing overruns, partially offset by revenue recognition on our 45% share of the GPS III follow-on constellation for the U.S. Space Force. Integrated Propulsion margins jumped to 12.7% from 11.8%, fueled by aftermarket service growth on our TF-39 engine fleet for the C-5M Galaxy sustainment program—up 15% year-over-year—and efficiencies from additive manufacturing initiatives that cut turbine blade production costs by 18%.

Regionally, U.S. DoD-funded programs contributed 68% of segment revenue with blended margins of 15.1%, while international sales—led by F-35 Lot 15 wing production exports to allies like Israel and Japan—delivered 16.4% margins, aided by favorable foreign exchange hedges. Looking ahead, we expect gross margins to expand another 50 basis points in the second half to 14.7%, supported by low-rate initial production ramps on our hypersonic boost-glide vehicle for the Army's Long-Range Hypersonic Weapon program and supply chain normalization post-Ukraine-related disruptions.

Turning to operating margins, we reported 11.8%, up 90 basis points from 10.9% last year and exceeding our guidance by 30 basis points. This was driven by gross margin leverage, coupled with SG&A discipline at 4.2% of sales—down from 4.5%—as we realized $120 million in annual run-rate savings from our Enterprise Resource Planning modernization and zero-based budgeting. R&D investment remained robust at 3.1% of revenue, or $315 million, focused on digital engineering twins for our sixth-gen fighter collaborative combat aircraft demonstrators and AI-enabled mission planning software, positioning us ahead of competitors like Boeing and Northrop Grumman in the Replicator initiative.

Operating expenses grew only 4% year-over-year despite inflation, thanks to headcount optimization in non-core functions and insourcing of lower-tier IT services. Segmentally, Defense Systems operated at 12.9% margins, Space & Launch at 10.6%—reflecting higher business development spend for NASA's Artemis lunar lander bids—and Propulsion at 11.2%. Corporate unallocated expenses improved 15% due to lower pension costs under CAS 408 recovery. For the full year, we now guide operating margins to 11.5-11.8%, up from our prior 11.2-11.5%, assuming stable labor markets and no material EAC changes on our top 10 programs, which represent 65% of backlog.

Net income came in at $850 million, or $3.25 diluted EPS, a 12% increase from $760 million or $2.90 last year. This reflects the operating strength, a lower effective tax rate of 19.2%—benefiting from R&D tax credits on our hypersonics portfolio and the extension of the TCJA provisions—and net interest expense of $45 million, down due to $1.2 billion in debt refinancing at sub-4% rates. Non-operating items included a $25 million gain from the sale of legacy missile tooling to Raytheon. Adjusted EPS, excluding one-time items, was $3.28, beating consensus by $0.08.

These metrics underscore our resilience amid macroeconomic headwinds like persistent inflation in rare earths and skilled labor shortages in the Sun Belt manufacturing hubs. Our focus on fixed-price incentives—now 55% of new awards—coupled with technical enablers like model-based systems engineering and advanced composites, is de-risking execution and driving margin accretion toward our long-term target of 15%+ operating margins by 2027. Geopolitically, elevated tensions in the Indo-Pacific and Ukraine are sustaining U.S. supplemental budgets, with our share of the $61 billion Ukraine aid package flowing through HIMARS MLRS sustainment.

Shifting to one of our most resilient segments, aftermarket and services revenue grew 18% year-over-year to $2.4 billion, representing 42% of our total revenue mix. This marks the sixth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth and underscores structural tailwinds as we navigate post-pandemic recovery in commercial aviation and sustained defense spending amid global geopolitical tensions.

In Commercial Aviation Aftermarket, which accounted for 62% of the segment total and grew 22% year-over-year to $1.49 billion, acceleration was fueled by a 15% increase in global flight hours, now back to 95% of 2019 levels according to IATA data, with widebody utilization on long-haul routes like Boeing 777 and 787 fleets surging 28% year-over-year. Our OEM-positioned services on CFM International LEAP-1A/1B engines for the Airbus A320neo family and LEAP-1B for the Boeing 737 MAX delivered 25% growth. We've seen strong pull-through from our installed base of over 5,000 LEAP engines in service, with shop visit rates stabilizing at 2.5% per 1,000 cycles—below our historical average—thanks to our proprietary Prognostics Health Management systems, which leverage AI-driven predictive analytics to reduce unplanned removals by 30%.

On the engine MRO side, our state-of-the-art facility in Singapore, expanded last year with a $250 million investment, hit 95% capacity utilization, processing over 120 LEAP modules per month. This regional hub has been critical for Asia-Pacific carriers, where aftermarket revenue jumped 32% year-over-year, driven by fleet expansions at IndiGo, AirAsia, and Lion Air, all heavy A320neo operators. In North America, we've secured multi-year TrueChoice Overhaul contracts with Delta and United, extending our book-to-bill ratio in commercial services to 1.3x.

Defense Aftermarket and Services rose 12% year-over-year to $910 million, or 38% of the segment. Growth was anchored by sustainment contracts on the F-35 Lightning II program, ramping to $450 million in annualized revenue through Lockheed Martin teaming agreements. Block 4 upgrades and ALIS/ODIN sustainment logistics drove a 16% uptick in depot-level repairs, with our Fort Worth facility achieving 98% on-time delivery against USAF SLAs. Missile defense programs, including PAC-3 MSE interceptors for the Patriot system, contributed another 14% growth, bolstered by $1.2 billion in new IDIQ task orders from the U.S. Army amid Ukraine-related replenishment demands.

Regionally, U.S. DoD spending remains our bedrock, up 10% year-over-year, but we're seeing inflection in Europe—up 25%—with NATO allies like Poland and Germany accelerating F-35 inductions and Eurofighter Typhoon MRO needs. In the Middle East, services on F-15QA for Qatar and Saudi fleets grew 20%, supported by our new Abu Dhabi repair center JV with EDGE Group.

This growth reflects our 'Services First' initiative, launched in 2022, shifting our aftermarket mix toward higher-value digital services—now 28% of revenues, up from 18% two years ago. Initiatives like our AeroEdge platform, integrating IoT sensors with digital twins for real-time fleet health monitoring, have boosted customer retention to 98% and upsell rates by 15%. We've also invested $400 million in capacity expansions, including a new composites MRO line in Mobile, Alabama, targeting Boeing 787 dreamliners, positioning us to capture share in the $120 billion global MRO TAM through 2030, per Oliver Wyman forecasts.

Looking forward, we expect aftermarket and services to grow 16-20% in FY24, with Q4 acceleration from holiday-season flight hour peaks and new F-35 LRIP 15 lot awards. Margins expanded 220 basis points to 32.5%, reflecting operating leverage and pricing discipline amid easing supply chain pressures on titanium forgings and nickel alloys.

Before moving on, a key leading indicator is our backlog growth. Total backlog stood at $152.4 billion at quarter-end, up $21.7 billion in absolute terms from $130.7 billion a year ago—that's a robust 16.6% year-over-year increase. On a quarter-over-quarter basis, we added $8.2 billion net, bringing funded backlog to $48.6 billion and unfunded to $103.8 billion. This marks our strongest backlog growth in five quarters, outpacing peers like Lockheed Martin and Boeing Defense, Space & Security.

By core segments: Aeronautics, 52% of backlog, grew by $9.8 billion or 18.2% year-over-year to $64.1 billion. The F-35 Lightning II program secured an additional $4.2 billion in low-rate initial production Lot 16 awards from the Joint Program Office, including TR-3 configurations with enhanced electronic warfare suites. International demand remains a tailwind—we booked $2.1 billion in Foreign Military Sales from NATO allies, including Finland's full-rate production tranche and Poland's follow-on block buy. Indo-Pacific tensions accelerated orders; Japan exercised options for 12 more F-35Bs worth $1.3 billion. Early wins on Next Generation Air Dominance digital engineering prototypes added $1.4 billion in concept refinement contracts.

Missiles and Fire Control, 28% of backlog, rose $7.4 billion or 22.1% year-over-year to $41.2 billion. Hypersonics drove this—our AGM-183A Air-Launched Rapid Response Weapon captured $3.1 billion in multi-year procurement from the USAF, building on successful glide body tests. Precision-guided munitions like JASSM-ER and Long-Range Anti-Ship Missile added $2.5 billion, fueled by Ukraine supplemental funding and Middle East FMS; Saudi Arabia inked $1.2 billion for integrated air defense upgrades amid Houthi threats. Our win rate hit 68%, above target, thanks to additive manufacturing for solid rocket motors, shaving 15% off production timelines.

Rotary and Mission Systems, 12% of backlog, increased $2.9 billion or 14.7% year-over-year to $22.6 billion. CH-53K King Stallion heavy-lift helicopters drove $1.6 billion from USMC full-rate production Lot 2, with enhanced survivability features like directed energy weapon integration. Germany's Sikorsky selection added $800 million. We're leveraging IDIQ vehicles like the Army's Future Long-Range Assault Aircraft framework.

Space, 8% of backlog, surged $1.6 billion or 25.4% year-over-year to $24.5 billion—our fastest-growing segment. Proliferated LEO constellations are key: we won $2.8 billion prime on a classified SATCOM relay for the Space Development Agency's Transport Layer Tranche 2, incorporating optical inter-satellite links. Commercial offsets include $900 million from Blue Origin on New Glenn heavy-lift boosters and NASA Artemis lunar lander sustainment. AUKUS Pillar II collaborations contributed $500 million in collaborative combat aircraft demos.

This backlog expansion underscores our supply chain resilience program, mitigating disruptions through dual-sourcing titanium forgings, enabling 12% faster award-to-delivery cycles; digital twin acceleration, unlocking $1.2 billion in performance-based logistics contracts for F-35 sustainment; and international diversification, with non-US backlog now at 28%, Asia-Pacific at 11%, and Europe at 10%. We expect backlog conversion to drive 8-10% organic revenue growth in FY24, with book-to-bill above 1.2x.

Our R&D investments remain the cornerstone of long-term growth, with $1.45 billion allocated through the first half of FY2024—up 18% year-over-year and representing 12.5% of trailing twelve-month revenues. This positions us ahead of the industry average, reflecting commitment to outpacing peers in next-generation capabilities.

By pillars: next-generation platforms at 55% or $800 million; advanced technologies at 30% or $435 million; enabling ecosystem at 15% or $215 million. Air dominance platforms received $450 million, up 22% year-over-year, with TRL 7 on our loyal wingman drone for manned-unmanned teaming, mirroring USAF NGAD requirements and positioning for the $20 billion CCA contract. Early flight tests demonstrated 95% mission success in peer contested environments, reducing pilot risk by 40%.

Space systems got $250 million for resilient LEO architectures, with optical inter-satellite links and radiation-hardened GaN electronics cutting latency by 30% in TacSat-Next. This aligns with Space Force's $18 billion budget; our LEO mesh secured $450 million IDIQ with INDOPACOM. Maritime platforms: $100 million on USVs and undersea drones with MOSA, hitting milestones in hypersonic integration for Virginia-class subs at Mach 7+ speeds and 2,500 nm range.

Advanced technologies: hypersonics $180 million, scaling scramjet to TRL 8 with 15% thrust gains via CMCs for LRHW, on track for $2.5 billion production. Directed energy $120 million, with 300 kW fiber laser at 50% efficiency for F-35 pods. Autonomy/AI $135 million, digital twins cutting F-35 sustainment 25%, leveraging OMS for 50% faster inserts.

Ecosystem: $100 million fortifying materials supply chains for titanium and rare earths, qualifying domestic CMC suppliers to cut lead times 35%. U.S. at 70%, Europe 15% via FCAS teaming, Asia-Pacific 10% for MQ-9 exports. Projected 3.5x ROI, 47 patents YTD, five DARPA CRADAs. We've upskilled 2,500 engineers to counter talent shortages.

Finally, revenue by segment: Commercial Aerospace $9.2 billion, +28% year-over-year, with 145 NovaJet NX-400 deliveries, up from 112, amid OEM ramp and 15% sequential build rate increase. Aftermarket parts +12% to $1.8 billion. North America 55% of growth, Asia-Pacific +45%, Europe +18%. SAF-ready deliveries at 20%.

Defense $6.8 billion, +9%, with F-47 Lightning II $2.4 billion, hypersonics $1.2 billion, international +20%. U.S. DoD 68%, Europe +25%.

Services $2.7 billion, +15%, MRO on CFM56/LEAP driving growth, digital prognostics securing ESAs. Margins 28%.

This momentum underscores our dual-exposure strength, raising full-year guidance.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Sarah. Operationally, we have seen significant improvements in our supply chain management, allowing us to increase production rates on key programs like the F-35 Lots and Vulcan Centaur. We are also investing in automation and digital technologies to improve efficiency and reduce costs. Specifically, our supply chain resilience efforts have dual-sourced critical materials like titanium forgings, shortening lead times by 12%, while additive manufacturing has reduced turbine blade costs by 18% and enabled faster hypersonic prototyping. Our Singapore and Abu Dhabi MRO hubs are at high utilization, supporting regional growth, and digital twins are optimizing F-35 logistics for better on-time delivery.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from Josh Cohen with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Josh Cohen:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the drivers behind the gross margin expansion and operating margin outperformance this quarter?

David Johnson:
Certainly, Josh. As Sarah detailed, the 70 basis point gross margin expansion to 14.2% came from strong execution on defense fixed-price contracts with favorable EAC adjustments totaling $2.4 billion, plus supply chain mitigations like Eastern European dual-sourcing that cut titanium variances by 12%. Operating margins hit 11.8% thanks to SG&A leverage from ERP savings and robust R&D positioning us for Replicator wins. We're guiding further H2 expansion to 14.7% gross on hypersonic LRIP ramps.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Rivera with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Rivera:
Hi, thanks. I'm curious about the sustainability of aftermarket and services growth at 18% year-over-year—any risks to that trajectory?

Sarah Lee:
Emily, great question. This growth is highly recurring, with commercial up 22% on LEAP engine pull-through and 95% Singapore utilization for Asia-Pacific carriers like IndiGo. Defense at 12% is anchored by F-35 sustainment and Patriot IDIQs. Our AeroEdge digital platform drives 98% retention and 15% upsells, with margins at 32.5%. We see 16-20% FY24 growth from F-35 lots and flight hour peaks.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Raj Patel:
Regarding the R&D investments—how do you think about ROI on next-gen platforms like CCA and hypersonics amid FY25 budget risks?

Lisa Patel:
Raj, our $1.45 billion R&D—12.5% of revenues—targets 3.5x ROI, with CCA at TRL 7 showing 95% mission success and hypersonics scaling scramjets for $2.5 billion awards. Digital twins and DEWs like 300 kW lasers de-risk execution. Diversification to Europe/Asia hedges U.S. risks, with 47 patents and DARPA CRADAs accelerating wins.

David Johnson:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I'm confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We remain focused on our strategic priorities, operational excellence, and innovation.

John Smith:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.

FY24 growth expected at 16-20%. (Note: Later mention of Services $2.7B +15%, possibly broader category.)
